scene ayaneandthetent1
: I’ve been waiting.
: You look like you’ve just seen a ghost.
: I’m in no mood for jokes right now.
: I can see that. I wasn’t trying to make a joke, though.
: Is it really you? Are you really here?
: I think so? I can’t really remember getting here, but that’s become par for the course for situations like this.
: What’s the last thing you remember?
: I think-
scene mayakaraoke32
scene ayaneandthetent1
: Talking to Maya...outside of the karaoke booth. Was that where it started this time? Did we all black out?
: Yes and no...I don’t remember leaving, but I do remember you acting strange before everything went to Hell.
: Well, what else happened while I was out? Have you found Maya yet?
scene ayaneandthetent2
: No...I haven’t. And I’m really not in any rush to tell you what happened after you came back into the room.
: That sounds...ominous.
scene ayaneandthetent3
: It was way worse than just ominous. It was terrifying. And even after all this time, I still can’t get it out of my-
: Wait, all this time? How long have I been gone?
scene ayaneandthetent4
: It’ll be thirty-five days since I woke up tomorrow. I think. I’ve been trying to keep track, but the clocks are acting...kind of weird.
: What?...
: I’ve been waiting all this time...
: It’s been thirty-five days and Maya isn’t here yet? The world hasn’t reset yet?
: No, but...Sensei...I don’t think this is like the other times we’ve done this.
: Yeah, I can tell by my month-long absence.
: That’s not what I mean. Even the way it started...it was nothing like the other times I’ve done this. And I want to think it was all just a...mirage, but...
scene ayaneandthetent5
: My clothes...when I woke up...
: They were still...They were covered in...in...
scene ayaneandthetent6
: Sensei, I’ve got a really bad feeling about all this.
: We need to find Maya.
: We can’t.
: What do you mean we can’t? We’ve done it before. We just have to-
: I mean we literally can’t leave. Everything outside of the school is gone. All we can do is wait for Maya to show up here. There’s no way we can go out and look for her.
: What do you mean everything is gone? That doesn’t make sense.
scene ayaneandthetent7
: Yeah! I know that! Nothing makes sense! And things already didn’t make sense before! But now they somehow make even less sense! I don’t know what else you want me to tell you!
: How about Makoto? Did she make it? Or...how about Sana? Is she here?
scene ayaneandthetent8
: Sana? Why would Sana be here?
: Because she-
scene escapetheroom40
scene ayaneandthetent8
: Because I-
: I’m not...really sure...
scene ayaneandthetent9
: No one’s here but me and you...and I’m sorry to say this when I promised to be more optimistic, but I’m not feeling very hopeful that anyone else will be showing up any time soon.
: Maya will be here. She’s always here. She’s the one who-
: I told you, Sensei. Things are different this time. This isn’t what we’re used to.
: Just think about it. Maya didn’t even realize this was coming. She always knows when this is coming, doesn’t she?
: Maybe that...weird feeling we had was what she normally feels when a reset is approaching? And we just didn’t realize it because it’s never happened to us before.
: No way...There’s no way she’d be able to keep her cool if she was going through something even remotely similar to-
: Something I’ve learned this apocalypse is that Maya can “keep her cool” no matter what happens. And I’d be lying if I said that didn’t terrify me.
: Why would-
: If you saw what I saw, you’d understand.
: But I’m glad you didn’t.
: Because I don’t think you’d ever be able to forget it.
scene black
Ayane grabs me by the hand and pulls me out into the hallway, where the blinding blue glow of a disappearing world begins to swallow me whole.
Maya will be here. I know she will.
And I’m not just saying that because I love her — I’m saying it because that is what needs to happen in order for all of this to play out the way it’s supposed to.
Her presence has been the only constant I’ve had throughout these many horrifying trips back to the beginning of our timeline.
And in a world that’s always repeating itself, I know she’s bound to as well.
So even if Ayane is right and everything is different this time, it won’t be different enough.
I need to remain hopeful when no one else is.
And I need to ignore the voices in the back of my mind that refuse to release their grip on it.
Because I may not have been able to take something that doesn’t belong to me, but I’ll be damned if I don’t take back something that should have been mine from the start.
scene ayaneandthetent10
: Ayane-
: I already told you, it isn’t possible to leave.
: Okay. Sure. But do you really need to squeeze my hand this hard?
scene ayaneandthetent11
: Fuck yes I have to squeeze your hand this hard! You really think I’m going to risk losing sight of you after worrying sick for over a month?! Not a chance!
: You’ll be lucky if I even let you go to the bathroom alone before the world resets.
: You have nothing to worry about. It’s not going to reset without Maya.
scene ayaneandthetent12
: I wonder if you’d still be saying that if you were the one waiting up there instead of me...
: Of course I would. I’m more experienced than you when it comes to this stuff.
: Not by a lot.
: But enough to make you at least consider that I can kind of...help in some way, right?
: Help with what? All we can do is wait. No amount of planning or thinking is going to help get us out of a mess that defies all logic and science.
: Some problems just have to fix themselves or...stay broken forever.
: There has to be something we can do. I don’t want to risk Maya being stuck “asleep” again. Especially when you couldn’t even see her after the last time she disappeared.
: Then maybe we’ll get lucky and you’ll see her up there and we’ll all live happily ever after.

: Ayane, I get that it’s probably hard to be optimistic when you’ve been stuck here for over a month...but if you start losing it now, I will too. And we don’t have any time to waste on...mental instability.
: Well, let’s see if you can figure out a way to remain “mentally stable” once you see what I’ve been looking at for thirty-five days...
scene black
scene ayaneandthetent13
: I’m not really sure what I’m looking at right now.
: It wraps around the entire building.
: I felt like it was closing in at first, but I’m pretty sure that was just me having a perpetual panic attack.
: Have you tried going through it?
: I tried poking it since you can reach it from the front steps of the school, but doing that just sent me back up here.
: The pictures change every few hours, but I don’t think it’s, like...a puzzle or anything like that.
: I’ve been keeping track of them in a notebook to see if I can figure out if they mean anything, but I think it’s just the world being broken again.
: This is why I said you can’t leave. It’s not like the last few times where the sky gets all cool-looking and the rest of the city stays mostly the same.
: This time, it’s like the city doesn’t even exist. And that the world’s been whittled down to just the school.
: She’ll be here, Ayane.
: If you say so, Sensei.
: Do you want coffee or something? We’re probably going to be here for a while.
: Sure. If you’re running to Koi Cafe, I’ll take a Copyrighted Frozen Beverage.
: Lucky for you, I’ve set up my own Koi Cafe.
scene black
Ayane lets go of my arm for the first time since I opened my eyes or...regained consciousness or...whatever it is that happens when I snap out of reset-induced delusions.
It’s a little strange, though.
I feel like...I remember most of this one.
I remember being locked in a house.
I remember...being alone.
Delicious hot pot.
A girl who grew up.
scene papercity31
scene papercity32
scene papercity33
scene papercity34
scene papercity35
scene ayaneandthetent14
And...
And that’s it.
Nothing else happened.
: You’ve...made quite a home for yourself up here, haven’t you?
scene ayaneandthetent15
: It’s not like I had anything else going on. And you’d be surprised what you can find lying around the school.
: You’ve got electricity and everything.
scene ayaneandthetent16
: I do! And might I add that I’m extremely proud of myself for being able to lug multiple generators up three flights of stairs. Even if it did take an entire day.
: Well, at least you haven’t been sitting here doing nothing. I feel less bad about making you wait a month now.
scene ayaneandthetent17
: You should still feel very bad about that and you should never do it again. Because even if I have food and water, the library’s DVD selection is extremely lacking.
: Do you have any idea how many times I’ve watched the Breakfast Club now? Because it is a number I am not proud of, Sensei.
: My English has gotten better, though. So at least there’s that.
: Leave it to the almost-eternal optimist to find a silver lining in the picture-clouds of the apocalypse.
: It helps being a little insane too. I can’t imagine many people in my situation would have set up a base camp, but here I am.
: Your mild insanity is the only thing keeping me grounded right now, so thanks for that.
: You’re welcome.
: I can only imagine what you had to go through to make it here, but I’m glad you did.
: Like I said, though. All there is to do now is continue playing the waiting game. I hope you like the Breakfast Club.
: You know...maybe I’ll take some coffee after all.
scene ayaneandthetent18
: It would be my pleasure, sir. Please take a seat inside our lovely triangular housing and I’ll have our wait staff bring it out right away.
: I even get to see your tent? You’re far too kind.
: Just wait until you see what other services we provide.
: This is probably the least appropriate it has ever been for you to hit on me.
scene ayaneandthetent19
: It’s been thirty-five days. Excuse me for getting a little excited.
: Now, go sit down so I can continue acting like your wife-slash-barista.
scene black
I climb into the tent and find there’s not much inside apart from a futon, a lamp, and a few notebooks Ayane’s been writing in.
It smells like her. Though, I guess that’s not surprising since she’s essentially been living here for over a month.
It’s comforting in a way that nothing ever is anymore. Especially nothing on this rooftop.
scene ayaneandthetent20
But even if that indiscernible flowery scent of perfume that she still wears despite what could have been indefinite loneliness clings to my nostrils, my heart can’t help but wander elsewhere.
Even now, in this claustrophobic polyester pyramid where the two of us are as close as we can be without staining the sheets, I’m thinking of someone else.
I’m worried about someone else.
And she knows it.
I know she knows it.

I can tell from the pheromones that have abandoned her body and flooded the tent. They dance in circles around the two pillows she dragged in here, yet she abstains from touching me because she cares.
And she doesn’t want to force something out of me when all I’ve ever done is force things out of her.
I’m sure she wouldn’t describe it that way if you asked her where her mind was. I’m sure she’d mention something about how easy it is to read me when I’ve always been her favorite book.
But if you ask me why she’s fascinated with martyrdom in a world without anyone to die for, I’d tell you it’s because she’s special.
That she’s a little insane.
And that there really isn’t anyone who would handle this the way she does.
: Can I ask you something, Sensei?
: Sure. What’s up?
: Just out of curiosity, if the world never resets and the two of us are stuck here for the rest of eternity, how long do you want to wait before we start repopulating the planet?
: Not the direction I expected this to go in.
scene ayaneandthetent21
: I think that’s a perfectly reasonable question! It’s our duty as Japanese citizens to procreate. Even when the rest of the world disappears.
: Your mind is everywhere but where it’s meant to be right now, isn’t it?
scene ayaneandthetent20
: Where would you say it’s meant to be?
: A way out....what we’re supposed to do next...anywhere but mindless fun and what-if scenarios.
: Doing that would drive me even more insane. Besides, I’ve more than paid my dues when it comes to critical thinking over the last month.
: Now that you’re here and we can be together again, I kind of just want to...go back to normal for a little while. Because who knows if we’ll ever be able to do that again?
: You look upset. How come?
: Ayane, when you were...feeling “weird” the day of the Halloween party...were you, like...hearing things?
: You mean like voices?
: Exactly. Does that mean you were?
: Were you?
: I asked you first.
: And I made you coffee.
: Then...yeah. I was.
: Haven’t you always, though?
: I know you’ve had stuff like that going on forever. And I know that’s why your bond with...Ami has...gotten so strong.
: Not like this. This time was different.
: I’m not surprised. Everything about this time is different. And, apart from being able to hang out in a tent with you, none of it’s really good.
: Were they saying anything specific?
: You don’t have to tell me if you don’t want to. I get it.
: It’s less that I don’t want to and more like I...feel like I’m not supposed to.
: All rules get thrown out the window when the world is ending, Sensei. You can say or do anything you want here.
: I think this might be my last reset.
scene ayaneandthetent22
: ...what?
: I keep...hearing this message that...if I don’t “take something that doesn’t belong to me,” something will be taken from me instead.
: What does...that mean?
: I’m not sure, but...I have an idea. The point is, though, time is up.
: I had until the end of summer and, if you hadn’t already noticed, I think that time has come.
: Wait, hold on. So, it’s...just because of that voice thing that you think you’re not going to make it through this reset? How did you come to that conclusion?
: I wouldn’t call it a conclusion. It’s more like a feeling. Like I was put here for some sort of purpose and, if I’m not going to fulfill it, there’s no reason for me to exist at all.
: Why do you need to have a purpose? Why can’t you just...be you?
: I wish I had an answer to that.
: No...you don’t. Because you don’t need to have an answer to that.
: Who cares if you’re not fulfilling your purpose? Just live happily and let everything else fall into place after that.
: But the voice-
: You think you’re the only person to hear a voice like that? One that tells you you’re not good enough and that you need to be someone else? Everyone hears that.
: I...okay. Sure. But I feel like the way this one is being delivered to me is a little different than the idea of everyone feeling subconsciously incomplete.
: That’s not what I-
scene ayaneandthetent23
: Hah...
scene ayaneandthetent24
: Okay. Yeah. I may have...inadvertently sounded a little preachy and generic just now. And I get that that doesn’t compare to what you are personally going through.
: But I’ve been hearing things too, Sensei. Actual voices. That want me to do things for them that I don’t want to do. And Ami heard...hears them too.
: What? Then...why haven’t you ever said anything?
: Uhh...because it’s creepy and totally fake?
: I just ignore them and nothing bad ever happens to me. Well, apart from being sucked into the apocalypse and being forced to watch the Breakfast Club over and over.
: You’re getting scared for no reason. And you’re scaring me by saying things like “This might be my last reset” when that’s completely untrue.
: It’s never over until it’s over. And you’re better than giving up just because the angel on your shoulder hates you even more than you do.
: You’re gonna be okay. We’ll get through this together.
: And if we don’t?
scene ayaneandthetent25
: If we don’t, then I’m definitely jumping on your replacement ASAP and having as many babies as possible.
scene ayaneandthetent26
: Oh, come on. I’m obviously kidding.
: If we don’t, I’m sure one of us will figure something out.
: Maybe it’s me. Maybe it’s you. Maybe it’s Maya. Maybe it’s someone completely unexpected. And maybe it takes another thousand or...million years or whatever.
: Predicting the future sucks because all it really does is make the present more nerve-wracking. And the present for us kind of sucks to begin with.
: So just...worry about today. Then, when you wake up in the morning, you can worry about tomorrow.
scene ayaneandthetent27
: Which, by then, would also be today. But I think you get what I’m saying.
: Yeah...
: I think I get what you’re saying.
scene ayaneandthetent20
: Great.
: Then, please excuse me while I take a much needed nap.
scene black
: Ayane-

: Don’t worry. You can keep talking to me. I just want to rest my head on your lap for a little while. I’ve been extremely Sensei-deprived lately and if I don’t do something about it now, I’m going to die.
scene ayaneandthetent28
: Are you happy now?
: I missed this.
: I missed you too.
: No you didn’t. You were too caught up in blackout-mode to miss me.
: In fact, the only reason I found you in the first place was because I heard banging in one of the classrooms when I went to get some more supplies. You’re lucky I didn’t bring my gun.
: I think calling either of us lucky in any regard can’t possibly be accurate when we have to go through things like this.
: And I think you’re wrong. Because we’re definitely lucky to have met each other.
: And we’re definitely lucky to have fallen in love.
: I’m so happy you’re back.
scene black
: Me too.
